subject.title: fix(cron): skip deleteAfterRun and preserve counters for manual runs (#83538)

question: Should every operator-triggered cron run be non-consuming for scheduler state and alerts, while timer and Gateway watcher-terminal runs remain consuming?
rationale: The linked report clearly supports preserving deleteAfterRun jobs, but this PR also changes retry counters, backoff, auto-disable, next-run timing, and failure-alert ownership for all operator outcomes; that broader policy needs explicit owner confirmation.

options.title: Adopt non-consuming operators
options.body: Treat every CLI/RPC operator run as observational execution only, while keeping timer and internal watcher-terminal runs scheduler-owned.

options.title: Limit to one-shot deletion
options.body: Prevent operator runs from consuming deleteAfterRun jobs but retain selected existing counter, backoff, or alert mutations.

recommendation.title: Adopt non-consuming operators
recommendation.body: Treat every CLI/RPC operator run as observational execution only, while keeping timer and internal watcher-terminal runs scheduler-owned.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest merged history for manual-run, retry, backoff, replay, and failure-alert semantics points to Takhoffman.
